_readme: THE FEE REGISTER — what each rail and each store takes from a sale, as dated reads of the vendor's own published page.
WHY IT EXISTS. Until 2026-09-29 no tool computed what a sale NETS on a channel. The store column of the price
register (services/platform/src/app-config-data.json `prices`) is graded by ADR 093 section 2's x1.20 ratio, and the
nets that ratio exists to protect lived as hand arithmetic in ADR 093 section 3 and as prose in
tooling/channel-register.json, and both had drifted: the channel register quoted a retired annual price and a
blended Paddle percentage, and one ADR 093 net could not be reproduced from the published Paddle fee at all.
EVERY CELL IS {value, asOf, verify}, plus `source` (the page read) and `quote` (its words, verbatim). `asOf` is the
instant the page was read; `verify` is the command that re-reads it, so a cell is re-checked by running a line
rather than by trusting this file. A cell is edited only after such a read, never to make a net come out right.
READ BY tooling/catalog/render-rail-prices.mjs `--net-sheet`: it applies these cells to the price register and
prints the net of every plan on every channel of tooling/channel-register.json that sells. `--net-sheet --check`
exits 1 when a cell it needs has a null value, or when a channel that can sell nets below the web row of the same
plan. And by tooling/ci/assert-small-business-program.mjs, which refuses a real App Store submission while
`apple-small-business-enrolment` carries no owner-attested date.
`apple-small-business-enrolment` IS NOT A FEE, AND ITS NULL IS NOT A GAP IN THIS FILE: it is the owner's step
(owner queue A-18: console-only, Account-Holder-only). It selects which Apple cell the net sheet applies, and it is
the one cell a human, not a page read, fills: the owner writes the day Apple APPROVED the enrolment, as the console shows it.
Not the day it was requested: Apple adjusts proceeds 15 days after the end of the fiscal month of APPROVAL (the cell's `quote`).
NOT MODELLED, AND SAID SO: Paddle's currency-conversion margin (none applies to a USD price charged in USD; an
INR charge through Paddle is not sold), store tax on a USD storefront price (US prices are tax-exclusive), and the
store INR columns, whose GST treatment differs per store and has not been read; the net sheet prints INR only for
the India web book, where Nikatru is the seller of record and ADR 076 section 10.1 fixes the treatment.

paddle-checkout.verify: curl -sL https://www.paddle.com/pricing | sed 's/<[^>]*>/ /g' | tr -s ' \n' ' ' | grep -o '5% + 50¢ per Checkout transaction'

value.basis: pay-as-you-go: this account holds no custom-pricing agreement, so a sale under the threshold is charged the published rate above. No sub-$10 quote has been asked for.

paddle-under-10.quote: If you’re selling products under $10 or require invoicing contact us for custom pricing
paddle-under-10.verify: curl -sL https://www.paddle.com/pricing | sed 's/<[^>]*>/ /g' | tr -s ' \n' ' ' | grep -o 'selling products under \$10 or require invoicing contact us for custom pricing'
paddle-under-10.ownerStep: Asking Paddle for custom pricing is a vendor contact the account holder makes (AB-M5-03, ADR 093's sub-$10 reopen trigger). A quote, when one comes, replaces `value` with its own read and date.

apple-iap-standard.quote: During a subscriber’s first year of service, you receive 70% of the subscription price at each billing cycle, minus applicable taxes.
apple-iap-standard.verify: curl -sL https://developer.apple.com/app-store/subscriptions/ | sed 's/<[^>]*>/ /g' | tr -s ' \n' ' ' | grep -o 'you receive 70% of the subscription price at each billing cycle'

apple-iap-small-business.quote: If you’re currently enrolled in the App Store Small Business Program, you receive 85% of the subscription price at each billing cycle (minus applicable taxes), regardless of whether or not the subscription has accumulated one year of paid service.
apple-iap-small-business.verify: curl -sL https://developer.apple.com/app-store/subscriptions/ | sed 's/<[^>]*>/ /g' | tr -s ' \n' ' ' | grep -o 'you receive 85% of the subscription price at each billing cycle'

apple-small-business-enrolment.source: Apple email "Welcome to the App Store Small Business Program." sent 2026-09-25T20:03:46Z to the Account Holder at nikatru.com (the APPROVAL notice; read by lead 7185eb 2026-10-03), and the owner attestation in chat 2026-10-03; the owner reads it in App Store Connect, Account Holder only (owner queue A-18); the timing rule from https://developer.apple.com/app-store/small-business-program/ (read 2026-09-30)
apple-small-business-enrolment.quote: Your proceeds will be adjusted fifteen (15) days after the end of the fiscal calendar month in which your enrollment is approved.
apple-small-business-enrolment.verify: The owner reads the Small Business Program status in App Store Connect and writes the day Apple APPROVED the enrolment (YYYY-MM-DD, a plain date, not the day it was requested) here; node tooling/ci/assert-small-business-program.mjs --for-submission=ios-appstore --real-submission then passes.
apple-small-business-enrolment.note: `value` is the APPROVAL date because Apple times the reduced commission from it: proceeds are adjusted 15 days after the end of the Apple fiscal month in which the enrolment is approved, so sales between approval and that day still pay the standard rate. The net sheet does not model that window.
apple-small-business-enrolment.ownerStep: A-18: enrol in the App Store Small Business Program. Console-only, Account-Holder-only, free. Record the day Apple APPROVES it, not the day it is requested. Until it is done a subscriber's first App Store year pays the standard rate, and a real App Store submission is refused.

play-billing-subscription.quote: Auto-renewing subscriptions (new & existing installs) ... First $1M (USD) of annual earnings 10% + 5% billing fee (EEA, UK and US from June 30, 2026); 15% for automatically renewing subscription products purchased by subscribers, regardless of revenue earned by the developer each year (all remaining markets)
play-billing-subscription.verify: curl -sL 'https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/112622?hl=en' | sed 's/<[^>]*>/ /g' | tr -s ' \n' ' ' | grep -o '15% for automatically renewing subscription products purchased by subscribers'

razorpay-platform.quote: The commercial model is strictly pay-as-you-go, you pay only the 2% transaction fee on successful payments.
razorpay-platform.verify: curl -sL https://razorpay.com/pricing/ | sed 's/<[^>]*>/ /g' | tr -s ' \n' ' ' | grep -o 'you pay only the 2% transaction fee on successful payments'

razorpay-subscription-add-on.quote: LIMITED TIME OFFER Standard Plan ~~0.9%*~~ 0.5%* Charged as an addon to every payment made towards a Subscription *Standard Platform Fee applies on the underlying payment. GST Applicable
razorpay-subscription-add-on.verify: curl -sL https://razorpay.com/subscriptions/ | sed 's/<s>/[struck]/g; s/<[^>]*>/ /g' | tr -s ' \n' ' ' | grep -o 'LIMITED TIME OFFER Standard Plan \[struck\]0.9%\* 0.5%\*'
razorpay-subscription-add-on.note: 0.9% is the list rate, struck through on the page; 0.5% is the offer. A reading of 0.9% as the rate charged (round-2 triage, AB-M5-04) came from a summarising fetch that dropped the strike-through. When the offer ends, `value.percentBps` becomes 90, and the India yearly net moves with it.

india-gst.quote: Razorpay's real cost is 2% platform plus a 0.5% subscriptions add-on, with the 18% GST on the fee returning as input tax credit.
india-gst.verify: grep -o 'with the 18% GST on the fee returning as input tax credit' tooling/legal/provider-register.json
india-gst.note: Nikatru is the seller of record on the India web book, so the INR web price carries 18% GST that Nikatru remits; the GST on Razorpay's fee returns as input tax credit, so the fee is netted at its pre-GST rate. The rate is the decision's, not a fresh read of a tax-rate text.

_why: The consumption tax a buyer's price can carry, per region, for the AI credit-pack floor (tooling/ops/port-switch.mjs C17, review 1 of #1136).

A store remits the tax inside the price before it takes its commission, so a floor that must hold in EVERY region is computed at the HIGHEST rate here; the India web book (razorpay, seller of record) uses IN's. Read only by port-switch: the net sheet's `cells` are untouched.
Each row is {value, asOf, source, quote, verify} like a cell. Add a region before selling into one with a higher rate; the floor rises with it.

IN.quote: Razorpay's real cost is 2% platform plus a 0.5% subscriptions add-on, with the 18% GST on the fee returning as input tax credit.
IN.verify: grep -o 'with the 18% GST on the fee returning as input tax credit' tooling/legal/provider-register.json

HU.quote: Hungary applies the highest standard VAT rate in the EU, at 27%.
HU.verify: curl -sL https://www.vatupdate.com/2026/02/11/hungary-comprehensive-vat-country-guide-2026/ | sed 's/<[^>]*>/ /g' | tr -s ' \n' ' ' | grep -o -i 'standard VAT rate[^.]*27%'
HU.note: A secondary source: the European Commission's rates table (Taxes in Europe Database) did not render rates without a query on 2026-10-02. 27% is the highest standard VAT rate in the EU, and the highest consumption tax among the App Store storefronts this table is used for.
